core_obligations: Set up the statement (proof lines 5186-5196): the author recalls that both sites carry structure sheaves and that the morphism is induced by the pullback of functions, so that the only thing to check is the locality condition at points.

Check locality at geometric points (proof lines 5196-5224): for a geometric point of X with image in Y, the induced map on stalks is the map on strict henselizations, which sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal because a germ vanishing at the image point pulls back to a germ vanishing at the point.
proof_roadmap: Recall the construction of the morphism of ringed sites and the locality condition.
Compute the induced map on stalks at geometric points.
Observe that the map on local rings is local, being induced by pullback of functions vanishing at the point.
difficulty_reason: The lemma verifies that the small morphism of ringed sites attached to a morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed sites (statement lines 5177-5184). The proof consists of identifying the locality condition with the corresponding statement about the induced map on stalks at geometric points (proof lines 5186-5196) and then checking that this map sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal, because a function vanishing at the image point pulls back to one vanishing at the point (proof lines 5196-5224). The non-formal content is the identification of the induced map on local rings with the map on strict henselizations. The claim is H2: one condition unpacked and verified.
